issues.description: Timeout-driven End frame races against in-flight Start/Text frames, corrupting the response bookend invariant.
issues.detail: _push_text_frame schedules a 1.0s timer to emit LLMFullResponseEndFrame while process_frame also emits one at end-of-stream. The timer can fire mid-await on Start/Text pushes, producing End-before-Text, double-End, or interleaved bookends on the next chunk. The stream has a deterministic end signal — emit Start before the loop, Text inside, End after, and drop the timer entirely.

issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer raises unhandled JSONDecodeError on non-JSON lines.
issues.detail: json.loads(response_line) has no try/except. A heartbeat, keepalive, malformed line, or error payload aborts the entire stream with an unhandled exception and leaves _output_response_open=True with a dangling close task. Either guard the parse and return None on failure, or document and enforce that transformers must be total over the input space.

issues.description: boto3 client is constructed and torn down per invocation inside process_frame.
issues.detail: The async with block creates a fresh bedrock-agentcore client for every LLMContextFrame, incurring TLS setup, credential resolution, and teardown on hot-path voice-pipeline turns. Create the client once at processor start (or lazily on first use) and reuse it. This separates connection lifecycle from request handling.

issues.description: agentArn parameter violates PEP 8 and the surrounding snake_case API convention.
issues.detail: Every other __init__ arg is snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region). agentArn is camelCase because it mirrors the AWS SDK field — but transport naming is an incidental detail of the wire format. Rename to agent_arn and map to agentRuntimeArn at the boto call site where the foreign convention actually lives.

issues.description: No exception safety around AgentCore invocation leaves bookend state corrupted on failure.
issues.detail: If invoke_agent_runtime or any async-for iteration raises, the Start frame may already be pushed, _output_response_open remains True, and _close_task remains scheduled. The next LLMContextFrame then pushes a second Start without a closing End. Wrap in try/finally that guarantees the bookend invariant on all failure paths.

issues.description: aioboto3 dependency bump bundled into the feature patch should be a separate commit.
issues.detail: pyproject.toml + uv.lock churn for aioboto3/aiobotocore/boto3/botocore/s3transfer is a dependency bump affecting every AWS consumer in the repo. It belongs in a separate patch with its own justification. Split it out and state whether the new processor actually requires 15.5.

synthesis.summary: The panel rejects the patch as currently structured. The dominant concern, flagged unanimously, is the timer-based response-bookend mechanism: a 1.0s asyncio.sleep races against the deterministic end-of-stream cleanup, producing double-End, interleaved Start/End, or wedged state, and a single unguarded json.loads in the default transformer turns any non-JSON line into a stream-killing exception that leaves the bookend state corrupted. Secondary but agreed: the boto3 client is rebuilt per invocation on a voice-pipeline hot path, and agentArn breaks the codebase's snake_case discipline at the public boundary. The fix is structural — emit Start before the loop, Text inside, End after, drop the timer, harden the parser, reuse the client, rename the arg, and split the dependency bump into its own patch.
